claim: The Cueva-Exposición del Queso Cabrales in Arenas de Cabrales runs ~45-minute guided tours (two 20-min segments), with adult tickets €6, child €4, groups (15+) €4.50, max 20 people per tour, reservations by phone 985 84 67 02; cave is 10–15°C so bring layers.
quote: Approximately 45 minutes ... Adults: €6.00 Children: €4.00 Groups (15+ people): €4.50 per person ... Maximum capacity: 20 people per tour ... Cave temperature: 10-15°C

claim: Arriondas to Arenas de Cabrales is about 37–38 km by road (~40 min), placing the Cueva-Exposición just outside the 30 km radius but still an easy half-day from Casa Marcial.
quote: 37 Km - Distancia entre Arenas de Cabrales y Arriondas

claim: The Museo de la Sidra in Nava (Plaza Príncipe de Asturias) charges €4 adult / €3 child 6–16 / €2 child 3–5, with free admission on Tuesdays; winter hours Tue–Fri 11:00–14:00 & 16:00–19:00, Sat 11:00–15:00 & 16:30–20:00, Sun 11:00–14:00.
quote: Adults: €4. ... Children ages 6-16: €3. ... Tuesdays are free (no reservations needed). ... Tuesday to Friday: 11:00-14:00 and 16:00-19:00. Saturday: 11:00-15:00 and 16:30-20:00.

claim: Arriondas to Nava is about 34 km by road, just outside the strict 30 km radius but still a comfortable day-trip for the Museo de la Sidra and town sidrerías.
quote: 34 Km - Distancia entre NAVA y arriondas asturias

claim: Escanciado is the signature Asturian pour: cider is poured from height so the stream hits the rim of the glass, releasing CO2 and aromas; served at 12–14°C in a fine-crystal cider glass (12 cm tall, 9 cm opening), and the resulting 'culín' is drunk in one go before the foam dies.
quote: Escanciar consiste en verter la sidra natural tradicional asturiana desde una cierta altura, desde la botella al vaso, logrando que el chorro impacte en el borde del vaso

claim: Sidraturismo Asturias' official booking platform lists llagar visits including Castañón (€3+ basic tour, €9+ Castañón Experience with cask sampling and snacks), Sidra Cortina (€10+), Llagar Herminio (€12–€30 including farm-to-table options), and Sidra Viuda de Angelón (€4.50).
quote: Llagar Castañón ... €3.00 ... V2. Castañón Experience €9.00+ ... Llagar Herminio €12.00-€30.00 ... Sidra Viuda de Angelón €4.50

claim: Llagar Castañón sits at Los Pisones 90, Quintueles (Villaviciosa concejo) — family tradition since 1938, modern facility from 2011, with three sidraturismo formats by reservation; technically outside the 30 km radius from Arriondas.
quote: Castañón es un llagar con tradición familiar desde 1938 ... Los Pisones 90, 33314 Quintueles, Villaviciosa

claim: Sidrería Prida in the centre of Nava is a traditional Asturian cider-house restaurant rated ~4.4/5, with menús around €20 featuring dishes like bacalao-and-shrimp scrambled eggs, hake, and braised kid goat alongside natural cider service.
quote: Sidrería Prida ... traditional Asturian cider house ... menus around €20 for high-quality dining

claim: Cangas de Onís hosts a Sunday market every week from roughly 09:30–13:30 around the Iglesia de Santa María, with artisan Cabrales, Gamoneu and Beyos cheeses, fabes (white beans), honey, cured meats, basketry and ceramics — a 200-year tradition and one of the most important markets in the Picos region.
quote: El mercado se celebra cada domingo ... cerca de la Iglesia Parroquial de Santa María ... quesos artesanos de Cabrales, Gamoneu y Beyos

claim: Nava's Festival de la Sidra Natural takes place the second weekend of July (10 July 2026) and the preceding week, culminating Sunday with the International Competition for Escanciadores — useful timing context for anyone visiting Asturias in early summer.

Official Asturian tourism guidance: cider is poured one culín at a time (about 100 ml), the drinker downs it immediately because aeration fades within seconds, and a small splash is traditionally tipped onto the floor to rinse the next person's rim of the glass.
quote: A guide to enjoying Asturian cider
